record.category: message queue broker: a vhost on a shared RabbitMQ broker

free_tier.stated: Little Lemur: 1 M messages a month, 20 connections, max 100 queues and max 10 000 queued messages on a shared RabbitMQ broker, free for as long as the instance is used, no card
free_tier.notes: The quota counts messages: a message counts once when it is published and once when it is consumed, so 1 M a month is about 500,000 messages that are both published and consumed. The monthly count resets on the first day of each month, and warning emails go out at 70 and 100 percent. An instance that crosses the queue or queued-message threshold is blocked from publishing and from creating queues. At the connection limit new connections are refused and existing ones stay up. Shared plans allow 200 channels per connection. An account may hold up to 49 free instances (650 once it has a paid instance).

retention.stated: A queue not consumed from for 28 days is deleted, temporary queues are deleted after 60 seconds, and a free instance with no message published or consumed during the latest two months is deleted after a warning email
retention.notes: Activity-based: an instance and its queues survive as long as messages move. The 28-day idle-queue limit is listed on the plans page for Little Lemur and was introduced on shared plans in 2017.

egress.terms: Data transfer is included within a fair-use allowance equal to 30% of the team's monthly spend; usage above it may be charged after a 30-day grace period
egress.free_allowance: unverified: the allowance is stated as 30% of team spend, and no page states a figure for a team that holds only free instances

record.interface_detail: Broker protocols AMQP 0.9.1 (ports 5672, and 5671 for AMQPS), AMQP 1.0, MQTT, STOMP, HTTP(S) and WebSockets; the interface vocabulary has no term for AMQP, MQTT, STOMP or WebSocket, so they are listed here. Instances, teams and keys are managed through the CloudAMQP Customer API at https://customer.cloudamqp.com/api, which answers 401 without an API key.
record.tooling: Any AMQP 0.9.1 client library, an MQTT or STOMP client, the CloudAMQP Customer API with an API key as the HTTP basic password, and the cloudamqp Terraform provider.
record.chaining: A durable work queue between a scheduler that publishes jobs and free compute workers that consume them, sized for about 33,000 message events a day.

limits.value: 1 M messages per month, counted on publish and on consume, reset on the first day of the month
queues idle for 28 days deleted; temporary queues deleted after 60 seconds; instance deleted after two months with no message

record.limits_note: 20 concurrent connections, max 100 queues and max 10 000 queued messages per instance, and 200 channels per connection. Crossing the queue or queued-message threshold blocks publishing and queue creation; at the connection limit new connections are refused. The vocabulary has no kind for a concurrency or a backlog cap.
record.binding_note: 1 M messages a month is about 33,000 a day (1,000,000 / 30), and a message that is published and consumed counts twice, so a steady job queue meets the monthly count before the 20-connection or 10 000-message backlog caps.

identity_cost.detail: The signup page asks for an email address, or a GitHub or Google sign-in; the plans page states no credit card is required for the free shared plans. The vendor's getting-started steps are create an account, choose a plan and create the instance, and name no phone step; whether the signup flow itself asks for a phone number is unverified: behind a sign-up.

record.reliability_note: A free instance with no message published or consumed for two months is deleted after a warning email; shared vhosts sit on a multi-tenant broker where other users' load can affect performance.
record.confidence_note: Every limit is quoted from a first-party page; the management API host was probed and answered 401 without a key. No broker connection was made, because a broker URL exists only inside an account. A probe of an AMQPS connection with an account's URL would move it to measured.

retention.stated: A free instance with no message published or consumed during the latest two months is deleted after a warning email; the plans page lists no idle-queue limit for Loyal Lemming
retention.notes: Activity-based: an instance survives as long as messages move, and the warning email offers to wake the instance up. The plans page listed Max idle queue time 28 days under Loyal Lemming in the archived copies of 2023-12-18 and 2025-08-03; the archived copy of 2025-11-18 and the current page list it under Little Lemur and Tough Tiger and not under Loyal Lemming. record.interface_detail: Broker protocols AMQP 0.9.1, MQTT, HTTP and WebSockets; LavinMQ supports neither AMQP 1.0 nor STOMP. A hosted LavinMQ instance has its own hostname, and its management interface is at https://{hostname}.lmq.cloudamqp.com. The interface vocabulary has no term for AMQP, MQTT or WebSocket, so they are listed here. The shared plans include streams, webhooks (push-queues) and the built-in delayed message exchange of LavinMQ. Instances, teams and keys are managed through the CloudAMQP Customer API at https://customer.cloudamqp.com/api.
record.tooling: Any AMQP 0-9-1 client library, many RabbitMQ-compatible ones included, an MQTT client, the CloudAMQP Customer API with an API key as the HTTP basic password and an empty username, and the cloudamqp Terraform provider, which names the plan lemming.
record.chaining: A durable work queue between a scheduler that publishes jobs and free compute workers that consume them, sized for about 66,667 message events a day; the larger of the two free CloudAMQP shared plans.

limits.value: 2 M messages per month, counted on publish and on consume, reset on the first day of the month
instance deleted after two months with no message published or consumed

record.limits_note: 40 concurrent connections, max 200 queues and max 20 000 queued messages per instance, and 200 channels per connection. At the connection limit new connections are refused. The vocabulary has no kind for a concurrency or a backlog cap.
record.binding_note: 2 M messages a month is about 66,667 a day (2,000,000 / 30), and a message that is published and consumed counts twice, so a steady job queue meets the monthly count before the 40-connection or 20 000-message backlog caps.

identity_cost.detail: The signup page asks for an email address, or a GitHub or Google sign-in, and an email signup is confirmed by a link sent to the inbox; the plans page states no credit card is required for the free shared plans. The vendor's steps for a LavinMQ instance are create the account, verify the email address and create the instance, and name no phone step; whether the signup flow itself asks for a phone number is unverified: behind a sign-up.

record.reliability_note: A free instance with no message published or consumed for two months is deleted after a warning email; a Lemming instance is a vhost on a multi-tenant LavinMQ broker that shares hardware with other instances, and the vendor lists the shared plans as not recommended for production because of variable performance.
record.confidence_note: Every limit is quoted from a first-party page; the management API host was probed and answered 401 without a key. No broker connection was made, because a broker URL exists only inside an account. A probe of an AMQPS connection with an account's URL would move it to measured.
record.notes: The other free CloudAMQP shared plan, Little Lemur on RabbitMQ, has half the quota and is a separate record. Paid shared LavinMQ (Elegant Ermine) is USD 19 a month for 20 M messages, 200 connections, max 2000 queues and max 200 000 queued messages. A shared LavinMQ instance can move to a single-node dedicated LavinMQ plan from the console, and it gets a new hostname.
